title: Ezekiel 25:8–17
context: The Lord GOD continues, now because Moab and Seir say, “Behold, the house of Judah is like all the nations.” The side of Moab will be opened from the frontier cities, “the glory of the country, Beth Jeshimoth, Baal Meon, and Kiriathaim,” and the children of the east will go against Ammon as well; Ammon will be given as a possession, and may not be remembered among the nations. Judgments will be executed on Moab, and they will know that he is the LORD. The three towns are named as Moab’s frontier glory; the verse does not map them further. The Lord GOD then speaks because Edom has dealt against the house of Judah by taking vengeance, has greatly offended, and has taken revenge, and the LORD’s hand will stretch out on Edom; man and animal will be cut off; the land will be desolate from Teman, and they will fall by the sword even to Dedan. Vengeance on Edom will be laid by the hand of the LORD’s people Israel, according to his anger and his wrath, and they will know his vengeance. A last word is spoken because the Philistines have taken revenge, with contempt of soul, to destroy with perpetual hostility. The LORD will stretch out his hand on the Philistines, cut off the Cherethites, and destroy the remnant of the sea coast. Great vengeance will be executed with wrathful rebukes, and they will know that he is the LORD when he lays his vengeance on them. The Cherethites are often taken as a Philistine group bound up with the sea coast; the oracle pairs them with that remnant and says no more.

verses.text: “ ‘The Lord GOD says: “Because Moab and Seir say, ‘Behold, the house of Judah is like all the nations,’
verses.arminianNotes:
The Lord GOD says, “Because Moab and Seir say, ‘Behold, the house of Judah is like all the nations,’” The offense is a saying: Judah is like all the nations, no different, no longer set apart. Moab and Seir are named together in the saying. Seir is often read as Edom’s country, already on the way to the later Edom word; the verse itself joins Seir to Moab in this one sentence.

Arminian readers hear a neighbor’s dismissal of Judah’s calling, a word that flattens the house into “all the nations,” and a charge the LORD takes seriously as spoken against his people.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers take the same saying of Moab and Seir, that the house of Judah is like all the nations, as the Lord GOD’s stated ground for the judgment that follows.

Shared ground: the taunt is that Judah is like all the nations. Moab and Seir are the ones who say it.

verses.text: therefore, behold, I will open the side of Moab from the cities, from his cities which are on its frontiers, the glory of the country, Beth Jeshimoth, Baal Meon, and Kiriathaim,
verses.arminianNotes:
“therefore, behold, I will open the side of Moab from the cities, from his cities which are on its frontiers, the glory of the country, Beth Jeshimoth, Baal Meon, and Kiriathaim,” The side of Moab is opened from the frontier cities, called the glory of the country, and three of them are named. The names stand as the pride of that border; exact locations are not given in the line itself.

Arminian readers hear an opening of Moab’s flank, a glory of cities exposed, a judgment that begins at the border they had thought a boast.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers take the opening of Moab’s side from the frontier cities, and the naming of Beth Jeshimoth, Baal Meon, and Kiriathaim as the glory of the country, as the LORD’s own first move against Moab.

Shared ground: the frontier glory is named, and the side is opened. The sentence runs on into the next verse.

verses.text: to the children of the east, to go against the children of Ammon; and I will give them for a possession, that the children of Ammon may not be remembered among the nations.
verses.arminianNotes:
The opened side is “to the children of the east, to go against the children of Ammon; and I will give them for a possession, that the children of Ammon may not be remembered among the nations.” The same eastern peoples already named against Ammon now come against Ammon again through Moab’s opened side, and Ammon is given as a possession, not to be remembered among the nations. The two neighbors are bound in one delivery.

Arminian readers hear Ammon’s name fading from the nations, a further answer to the “Aha!” and a possession handed to the east, a word that still explains why Moab’s border is opened.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers take the children of the east going against Ammon, and Ammon given as a possession so as not to be remembered among the nations, as the LORD’s appointed end for that people, reached through Moab’s opened side.

Shared ground: Ammon is given as a possession, and is not to be remembered among the nations. The east is the same agent already named.

verses.text: I will execute judgments on Moab. Then they will know that I am the LORD.”
verses.arminianNotes:
“I will execute judgments on Moab. Then they will know that I am the LORD.” Moab’s own judgments are stated in a short close, and the purpose is again that they know that he is the LORD. The saying that Judah was like all the nations is answered by a knowledge of the LORD in Moab itself.

Arminian readers hear judgments executed so that Moab knows the LORD, a purpose that treats even this neighbor as one who will come to that knowledge through the word that falls on them.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers take the execution of judgments on Moab, and the knowledge that he is the LORD, as his own end in the oracle.

Shared ground: Moab will know that he is the LORD. The formula closes the Moab word as it closed the word against Ammon.

verses.text: “ ‘The Lord GOD says: “Because Edom has dealt against the house of Judah by taking vengeance, and has greatly offended, and taken revenge on them,”
verses.arminianNotes:
The Lord GOD says, “Because Edom has dealt against the house of Judah by taking vengeance, and has greatly offended, and taken revenge on them,” Edom’s offense is vengeance taken against Judah, a great offense, revenge on the house already down. The charge is repeated in close words: taking vengeance, and taken revenge, and the greatness of the offense is named.

Arminian readers hear a neighbor who used Judah’s trouble as a time for revenge, a guilt of opportunity, and a word the LORD speaks as one who sees that revenge and answers it.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers take the same dealing against the house of Judah, the vengeance, the great offense, and the revenge, as the Lord GOD’s ground for stretching out his hand in the next verse.

Shared ground: Edom’s sin is vengeance against Judah. The sentence is the because; the therefore follows.

verses.text: therefore the Lord GOD says, “I will stretch out my hand on Edom, and will cut off man and animal from it; and I will make it desolate from Teman. They will fall by the sword even to Dedan.
verses.arminianNotes:
“therefore the Lord GOD says, “I will stretch out my hand on Edom, and will cut off man and animal from it; and I will make it desolate from Teman. They will fall by the sword even to Dedan.” The hand stretched out means a cutting off of man and animal, a desolation from Teman, and the sword as far as Dedan. Teman and Dedan mark the range of the blow, often taken as Edom’s extents; the verse names the two and does not describe their later history.

Arminian readers hear a land emptied of man and animal, from Teman to Dedan, a desolation that answers the revenge, and a word Edom can hear as the LORD’s own hand.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers take the stretched-out hand, the cutting off of man and animal, the desolation from Teman, and the sword to Dedan as the Lord GOD’s appointed judgment on Edom.

Shared ground: the hand is on Edom, and the sword runs from Teman to Dedan. The two place-names are the oracle’s own measure of the land.

verses.text: I will lay my vengeance on Edom by the hand of my people Israel. They will do in Edom according to my anger and according to my wrath. Then they will know my vengeance,” says the Lord GOD.
verses.arminianNotes:
“I will lay my vengeance on Edom by the hand of my people Israel. They will do in Edom according to my anger and according to my wrath. Then they will know my vengeance,” says the Lord GOD. The vengeance is the LORD’s, laid by the hand of his people Israel, who will do in Edom according to his anger and his wrath. The knowledge at the end is knowledge of his vengeance. Israel is the hand named in the verse, and the anger and the wrath remain his.

Arminian readers hear a vengeance that is the LORD’s, carried out by his people as the hand he names, a moral answer to Edom’s own revenge, and a knowledge of that vengeance as his.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers take the same laying of vengeance by the hand of his people Israel, the doing according to his anger and wrath, and the knowledge of his vengeance, as the Lord GOD’s own word.

Shared ground: the vengeance is his, and Israel is the hand. The traditions can share that ascription without a new dispute over the means.

verses.text: “ ‘The Lord GOD says: “Because the Philistines have taken revenge, and have taken vengeance with contempt of soul to destroy with perpetual hostility,”
verses.arminianNotes:
The Lord GOD says, “Because the Philistines have taken revenge, and have taken vengeance with contempt of soul to destroy with perpetual hostility,” The last because of the chapter is the Philistines’ revenge, taken with contempt of soul, aimed at destruction, and marked as perpetual hostility. The language of revenge and contempt recalls the words against Edom and Ammon, now applied to the coast.

Arminian readers hear a long hostility, not a single raid only, a contempt of soul that meant to destroy, and a charge the LORD draws from their own enduring enmity.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers take the revenge, the vengeance with contempt of soul, and the purpose to destroy with perpetual hostility as the Lord GOD’s stated ground against the Philistines.

Shared ground: the offense is revenge and perpetual hostility. The therefore of the next verses rests on that because.

verses.text: therefore the Lord GOD says, “Behold, I will stretch out my hand on the Philistines, and I will cut off the Cherethites, and destroy the remnant of the sea coast.
verses.arminianNotes:
“therefore the Lord GOD says, “Behold, I will stretch out my hand on the Philistines, and I will cut off the Cherethites, and destroy the remnant of the sea coast.” The stretched-out hand is on the Philistines; the Cherethites will be cut off, and the remnant of the sea coast destroyed. Many readers take the Cherethites as a Philistine group tied to the coast, perhaps to a western origin; the verse pairs them with the remnant of the sea coast and does not say more.

Arminian readers hear a judgment that reaches the coast remnant, a cutting off of the Cherethites, a word the sea peoples can recognize as the LORD’s answer to perpetual hostility.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers take the stretched-out hand, the cutting off of the Cherethites, and the destroying of the remnant of the sea coast as the Lord GOD’s appointed word against the Philistines.

Shared ground: the hand is on the Philistines, and the coast remnant is in view. The Cherethites are named with that remnant.

verses.text: I will execute great vengeance on them with wrathful rebukes. Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I lay my vengeance on them.” ’ ”
verses.arminianNotes:
“I will execute great vengeance on them with wrathful rebukes. Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I lay my vengeance on them.” Great vengeance and wrathful rebukes will be executed, and they will know that he is the LORD when he lays his vengeance on them. The knowledge of the LORD is again the end, now joined in so many words to the laying of vengeance.

Arminian readers hear vengeance and rebukes that lead to the knowledge of the LORD, a purpose that even this last neighbor will know him when the vengeance is laid, a close that matches the closes already spoken over Ammon, Moab, and Edom.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers take the great vengeance, the wrathful rebukes, and the knowledge that he is the LORD when he lays his vengeance, as his own end in the Philistine word.

Shared ground: they will know that he is the LORD when the vengeance is laid. The chapter of neighbor-oracles ends on that knowledge.
